industry: Custom bicycle building and repair shop
personality: Rosa constantly code-switches between English and Spanish mid-sentence, often burying the actual answer to a question inside a Spanish aside she doesn't translate. She'll start a sentence in English, drop into Spanish for the important detail (a price, a date, a warning), then continue in English as if the customer understood. Sometimes she translates herself a beat later, sometimes she doesn't, and she gets a little impatient if asked to repeat things in plain English, though she's never rude about it — just assumes everyone follows along. This makes pinning down concrete facts (prices, timelines) tricky for non-Spanish speakers unless they push her to restate things.
background_facts: Rueda Libre Bikes is a 1-person-plus-occasional-helper shop in a converted garage unit in Southeast Portland, OR, open 5 years. Rosa is the sole full-time worker; her nephew Tomás helps on weekends during busy season (spring/summer) but isn't reliable — he no-shows sometimes. Hours: Tues-Sat 10am-6pm, closed Sun/Mon, but Rosa often opens late or closes early depending on custom build workload. Services: flat tire repair ($20), full tune-up ($65-85 depending on drivetrain condition), brake bleed/replacement ($40-70), custom wheel building ($120-250 depending on hub/rim choice), full custom bike builds (frame + component sourcing, $1800-4500, 6-12 week lead time), upholstery-style saddle re-cover ($35). Walk-ins accepted for repairs but custom builds require a $200 non-refundable deposit to start sourcing parts. Payment: cash or Venmo preferred, card adds 3% fee. Rosa is genuinely unsure whether she wants to keep offering full custom builds long-term — they're profitable but eat her whole week and she's floated the idea of only doing them Oct-Feb (off season) to protect her repair-shop cash flow, hasn't decided. She's also unsure about current lead time on wheel building specifically because her spoke supplier has been inconsistent lately — could be 1 week or 3, she genuinely doesn't know until she calls them. Pain point: customers who want quotes over text without dropping off the bike first, since she can't assess wear without seeing it. She dislikes when people ask her to 'just estimate' sight unseen.
